NutriCore Foods Inc. - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriCore Foods Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriCore Foods' Q3 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Growth Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: gross margin analysis including drivers and trends, the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, the impact of new product innovations and launches, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, volume and price/mix analysis, performance in key channels like retail, foodservice, and convenience, EPS guidance and key assumptions, and organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year.

First, regarding gross margin analysis: drivers and trends—we expanded margins significantly through pricing and efficiencies, reaching 48.2% consolidated.

Second, concerning the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions—these headwinds persisted but were well-mitigated, limiting the drag on our results.

Third, in terms of the impact of new product innovations and launches—our pipeline drove meaningful incremental revenue and margin uplift.

Fourth, looking at discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies—our disciplined approach fueled organic growth while protecting profitability.

Fifth, reviewing volume and price/mix analysis—we balanced volume gains with strong price/mix tailwinds for robust top-line expansion.

Sixth, analyzing performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience—each channel showed resilience and growth acceleration.

Seventh, examining EPS guidance and key assumptions—we're guiding to solid growth with clear drivers across the P&L.

Eighth, considering organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year—we're raising our outlook, confident in sustained momentum.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3. Net sales were $4.85 billion, representing an 8.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 48.2%, impacted by moderating input costs offset by strong pricing and productivity. Operating income was $920 million, and earnings per share were $1.18. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $2.1 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for adjusted EPS of $4.65 to $4.85 and organic sales growth of 4% to 6%.

To give you more color on the eight areas Alex highlighted, let me start with gross margin analysis, drivers, and trends. Our gross margin performance continues to demonstrate the resilience of our portfolio and the effectiveness of our strategic initiatives amid a volatile input cost environment. For Q3, we delivered a consolidated gross margin of 48.2%, representing a 210 basis point expansion year-over-year from 46.1% and 50 basis points sequentially from Q2's 47.7%. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, underscoring the structural improvements we're embedding across our Snacks, Beverages, and Dairy segments.

Breaking this down by key drivers using our internal volume, mix, and price variance framework for COGS, pricing remains the standout driver, contributing approximately 320 basis points of expansion. We've successfully executed targeted price increases averaging 7-9% across our portfolio, with particularly strong traction in North America and Asia-Pacific. In Snacks, for instance, our premium chip lines—like the newly launched NutriCore Heritage Organics—saw list price hikes of 8.5% that were largely accepted by consumers, thanks to our strong brand equity and loyalty programs. In Beverages, functional hydration products saw 9.2% pricing, offsetting the 12% YoY cocoa cost inflation we've seen globally. Europe lagged slightly at 5% pricing due to heightened private label pressure from discounters like Aldi and Lidl, but even there, our RTD coffee platform held firm.

Product mix shift provided a solid 150 basis points contributor, driven by a favorable shift toward higher-margin premium and health-focused SKUs, which now represent 28% of our Snacks revenue—up from 22% a year ago. Plant-based dairy alternatives grew 18% in volume and boosted segment margins by 180 bps to 52.4%. In Beverages, low/no-sugar formulations like our ZeroWave line expanded to 35% mix share, commanding 15-20% price premiums over core CSDs. This trend is accelerating as consumers trade up amid health consciousness post-COVID, with Nielsen data showing a 14% category shift toward premium F&B in the US.

On the unfavorable side, input costs deducted about 180 basis points, primarily from commodity volatility. Cocoa prices surged 32% YoY due to poor West African harvests—impacting our chocolate-coated snacks by 4.2 percentage points. Dairy costs rose 11% on tighter global milk supplies from El Niño effects in Oceania, hitting our yogurt and cheese platforms. Freight and packaging added another 1.5 points, though ocean rates have stabilized 15% below Q1 peaks thanks to normalized Red Sea routing. Sugar and corn held steady, hedged effectively at 85% coverage for FY24.

Our technical initiatives offset 120 basis points of pressure. Plant automation yielded 2.5% COGS savings, with AI-driven yield optimization in our 15 North American snack facilities reducing waste by 8% on potato processing. Precision agriculture partnerships with suppliers, covering 40% of our grain inputs, improved harvest predictability and cut procurement costs 6%. Sustainable sourcing, including RSPO-certified palm oil at 95% compliance, avoided $12 million in penalties and premiums. Regionally, APAC efficiencies shone brightest, with Vietnam beverage plants achieving 3.1% savings via robotic palletizing, expanding local margins to 51.2% versus 47.8% globally.

Regionally, North America, at 62% of revenue, hit margins of 50.6%, up 280 bps YoY, fueled by robust pricing and mix in snacks and beverages, with US retail velocity remaining strong at +3.2%, outpacing IRI-tracked category growth. Europe, at 18%, saw 44.3% margins, flat YoY, pressured by 2% volume softness and private label share gains to 28%, but mitigated by 10% premium dairy growth in the Nordics. Asia-Pacific and LATAM, at 20%, reached 47.1% margins, up 190 bps, driven by 12% premium bev growth in India and China and hedging against LATAM grain inflation.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 gross margins of 48.5-49.0%, with full-year expansion of 250+ bps to ~48.0%. This trajectory is supported by our Margin+3 program: sustained pricing discipline via dynamic analytics, targeting 6-8% in FY25; $150 million in productivity from digital supply chain twins and supplier co-innovation; and portfolio optimization, pruning 5% of low-margin SKUs to fund premium R&D like fermented protein snacks. Risks include potential cocoa escalation to $4,500/ton if Ivory Coast yields disappoint, but our 70% forward hedging and diversified sourcing provide a buffer. In summary, our gross margin expansion reflects not just tactical wins but a durable competitive moat in an industry where input volatility averages 10-15% annually. We're positioning NutriCore Foods to outperform peers, targeting 52%+ margins by 2026 through premiumization and efficiency.

Next, on the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions—a key headwind top-of-mind for investors. The Food & Beverage sector has been navigating a perfect storm since early 2022—geopolitical tensions, extreme weather, and lingering pandemic aftershocks. For NutriCore, these pressures drove an 18% year-over-year increase in COGS, primarily from core commodities and logistics.

On input cost inflation, our basket of key inputs—wheat flour, sugar, dairy proteins, vegetable oils, and packaging materials—saw weighted average inflation of 22% YoY in Q3, up from 19% in Q2. Sugar prices surged 35% YoY, mirroring drought-hit harvests in Brazil and India, which account for ~60% of global supply, and we're a major buyer for beverages and snacks. Cocoa jumped 45% amid West African supply constraints. Dairy costs rose 25%, fueled by U.S. herd reductions and EU export curbs post-Russia-Ukraine escalation. Packaging like aluminum for cans increased 28% due to energy surcharges, PET resin for bottles climbed 20% on Asian petrochemical tightness, and energy added 15%.

Regionally, North America bore 55% of the impact with COGS inflation at 20% YoY, exacerbated by port congestion and labor shortages. EMEA was milder at 16%, but avian flu spiked poultry feed costs. Asia-Pacific saw the sharpest at 25%, driven by rice and palm oil inflation from El Niño and Indonesia's export bans. This translated to gross margin compression of 320 basis points YoY, from 36.2% to 32.9%, with pure input drag ~450 bps excluding pricing actions like our 8-10% beverage ASP increases.

On supply chain disruptions, while global container rates eased 40% from 2022 peaks, we're still facing 15-20% higher ocean freight versus pre-pandemic. Lead times for imported spices and tropical fruits from Southeast Asia stretched to 45 days, causing $12 million in inventory obsolescence and production idles. Air freight for perishables added $8 million in premiums, and U.S. Midwest trucking delays disrupted flour milling by 10-12%, compounded by port strikes and rail bottlenecks.

Our strategic response delivered $150 million in run-rate savings YTD: hedging 70% of 2024 wheat and sugar at fixed rates via Chicago Merc and ICE futures, shaving 8% off forward costs; long-term contracts with diversified suppliers reducing single-source risk from 40% to 25%; our AgriChain 2.0 blockchain platform integrated with SAP Ariba, cutting procurement cycles by 30%; nearshoring 15% of tropical fruit to Mexico; $25 million in U.S. vertical farms for herbs yielding 20% cost stability; SKU rationalization from 2,800 to 2,400 items focusing high-margin winners; AI-driven yield optimization improving input efficiency by 5-7%; pricing recapturing 60% of margin erosion; and regenerative ag partnerships stabilizing 10% of grain costs.

Forward, we expect input inflation to moderate to 10-12% YoY in Q4 and 8% in FY24 as La Niña eases yields and grain corridors stabilize. Supply chain frictions should fade, targeting 10% freight savings, positioning gross margins to rebound to 34-35% by year-end and supporting raised FY EBITDA of $1.2-1.25 billion. While these shaved ~200 bps off EBITDA margins, our playbook limited net EPS dilution to 4%, better than the industry's 7-10%.

Moving to the impact of new product innovations and launches—one of the key drivers behind our 12% YoY top-line growth. Innovation is a cornerstone of our Taste the Future strategy, investing heavily in R&D for functional beverages, plant-based snacks, and premium ready-to-eat meals. In Q3, our pipeline delivered $185 million in incremental revenue, 28% of total net sales growth, driving 150 bps gross margin expansion to 42.3%.

Standout was ZestPro Protein Shakes, RTD high-protein beverages with grass-fed whey isolate and adaptogenic mushrooms. Priced at $3.49 per 12-oz, targeting the $12 billion U.S. RTD protein market growing 15% CAGR per IRI, it posted 3x repeat purchase rate in 90 days, 2.1% dollar share in its subcategory, $72 million sales exceeding forecast by 18%, with 55% contribution margins from Wisconsin co-manufacturing.

Complementing was GreenWave Plant-Based Bites, using precision-fermented pea protein and upcycled almond pulp. Aligning with the $25 billion plant-based snack market by 2028 per Euromonitor, launched in 4,200 Kroger/Whole Foods doors, 22% household penetration, 14% lift in adjacent sales, $45 million revenue at 48% gross margin from fermentation tech reducing waste 35%.

Beverage side, QuenchZero Hydration—zero-sugar sparkling waters with nootropics—priced $2.29/can, $68 million sales, 31% YoY velocity in functional water, offsetting 5% soda contraction, boosting portfolio penetration 8 points.

Regionally, North America (62% innovation sales) drove 19% category share gain in health channels, market share to 7.2% in RTD proteins; EMEA (22%) topped €28 million with 16% UK/Germany growth; APAC 35% YoY, £420 million via Tmall/BigBasket, 40% trial-to-repeat.

Powered by $120 million R&D, AI flavor profiling with IBM Watson, 14-month launch timelines, 92% approval rates, carbon-neutral processes cutting Scope 3 22%, unlocking premium space. Focus on functional nutrition (45%), sustainability (30%), convenience (25%); household penetration up 11 points to 24%. Ahead, 12 SKUs like GLP-1 bars Q1 '25, guiding 30-35% FY25 growth, $750 million incremental at 50%+ margins. Our engine delivers outsized returns in a $4.5 trillion market.

On pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies—RGM continues to deliver resilient top-line amid macro dynamics. Organic net revenue grew 5.2% YoY, sixth straight quarter positive: 4.1% from pricing, 1.8% mix toward premium, offset by 0.7% volume headwind. Outperformed peers on price/mix by 150 bps.

Pricing cornerstone: targeted 6-8% list increases across beverages, snacks, ambient grocery, with EDLP on high-velocity SKUs. North America beverages (35% revenue) 7.2% on CSDs/functional waters, elasticity -1.2 vs category -1.5, passing 85% inflation from HFCS/aluminum. Snacks surgical 5.5% on savory, flat on healthier; 420 bps sequential margin to 42.1%, clawing 9% YTD inflation.

Three-pillar RGM—pricing, mix, volume—with analytics. Premium now 28% portfolio (up from 22%), grew 12%; VitalHydrate 15% functional share, plant-based dips 18% uplift; rationalized 12% SKUs since 2022. Volumes soft group-wide but e-com +14%, foodservice +3%; Zero Sugar +5% in NARTD.

Regionally: NA (55%) 5.3% pricing, club strength; EMEA 3.2% good-better-best; APAC/LATAM standouts 6.8%/7.5%. PROS Pricing AI simulates 10,000 scenarios/50k SKUs, 25% optimization; Kantar segmentation, Anaplan trade mgmt cut ineffective spend 18%. Aligns inflation pass-through (90% YTD), sustainability premium (8% WTP), omnichannel (22% sales). FY23 organic 4-6%, pricing 3-5%, mix/volume flat-+2%.

Now, volume and price/mix analysis: reported net revenues $4.8 billion, up 6.2% YoY; organic 8.0% ex-FX/divestiture. +2.4% volume, +5.6% price/mix—fourth straight positive volume.

Volumes: Beverages +2.1% (sparkling/functional +7.2%, CSD -1.5%); Convenience +3.0% (PretzelPop +12%); Nutrition +1.8%. NA +3.2% e-com 18%; EMEA flat; APAC +4.5%; LatAm -0.5%. Price/mix: ASP +4.2% from 5-7% hikes, mix +1.4% premium/BFY 42%; sparkling/energy gains.

Portfolio Power: 12 NPDs 70% BFY; sunset 8% SKUs; AI pricing 200 bps accretion. Q3 volume 2-3%, price/mix 4-5%.

Performance in key channels: 7.2% organic growth, strongest mix pre-pandemic. Retail (52%) 5.1%, volume +1.8%/price-mix 3.3%, share 14.2%, premium +12%, e-com +22% to 18%; NA 6.8%, APAC double-digit. Foodservice (28%) 9.4%, traffic +6.2%, volume +4.1%; US 11.2%. Convenience (20%) 12.7%, impulse +11%, US 14.9%. Balanced exposure 250 bps margin; FY 6-8% organic.

EPS guidance: FY24 adjusted $4.65-$4.85, 9-14% growth. Organic 6-8%: pricing 4-5%, volume/mix 2-3%. Gross 150-200 bps to 42.5-43.0% via $180M productivity, 75% hedges, premium shift. SG&A flat 24.0-24.2%, OpEx +5-6%. Tax 22.5-23.5%, FCF $1.4-1.6B. Vitality Forward: prune low-growth, 50% BFY by FY26.

Organic sales growth guidance: Q1 FY25 3-5%, FY25 raised 4-6%. Pricing 2-3%, volume 1-2% Q1/2-3% FY, mix 0.5-1. NA 4-6%, EMEA 3-5%, APAC/LatAm 5-7%. Innovation $250M R&D 25+ NPDs, supply resilience, route-to-market digital.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

Mike Johnson (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of input cost inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, Mike. As Jordan detailed, input inflation hit 22% weighted average on our key basket, with sugar up 35%, cocoa 45%, dairy 25%, but our hedging at 70-85% coverage and pricing pass-through of 70-90% limited the gross margin hit to manageable levels. We've clawed back most through efficiencies like AgriChain 2.0 and nearshoring, expecting moderation to 8-12% ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Lisa Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new product launches and what is the expected impact on growth?

Taylor Kim (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Lisa. Building on our Q3 successes like ZestPro at $72 million with 55% margins and GreenWave Bites, we're accelerating with 12 SKUs including GLP-1 companions and mycelium coffee. Expect 30-35% of FY25 growth from innovations, $750 million incremental at 50%+ margins, driven by R&D AI and 35% pipeline conversion, outpacing the category.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Barclays. Please proceed.

David Patel (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Morgan Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. Disruptions like 45-day lead times and $20 million in premiums were offset by blockchain traceability cutting cycles 30%, vertical farms for 20% stability, SKU trim to 2,400, and 70% localization. Freight easing 10%, with ERP AI reducing stockouts 40%, building resilience for FY25.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Rodriguez (Morgan Stanley):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Emily, for Q4 and full year, organic sales 4-6% with pricing 3-5%, volumes accelerating; gross margins 48.5-49.0%; EPS $4.65-4.85. Key assumptions: commodity moderation +3%, no recession, productivity $180M. Risks hedged, FCF strong for returns—confident in execution.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriCore Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
